quotes.text: Attach a customer to a Checkout Session after creation to support mid-checkout authentication.
enabling their saved payment methods, email, and billing information to automatically populate without losing any information the customer has already entered
Use this when you allow customers to begin checkout as a guest and then offer the option to log in during the checkout process.
To request access to this preview feature, enter your email below and a member of our team will contact you.

old_evidence.text: Attach a customer to a Checkout Session after creation to support mid-checkout authentication.
This is useful when you allow customers to begin checkout as a guest and offer the option to log in during the checkout process.

findings: The November raw lines 5-9 retains the April old raw lines 4-8 core behavior: a Customer can be attached to an existing Checkout Session after creation in a guest-to-login checkout, preserving entered information while populating saved payment methods, email and billing information.

The new raw lines 11-20 adds an explicit request-access preview gate. The current source lines 11-26 and route descriptions at wiki/stripe-index.md:88, wiki/companies/stripe.md:357 and wiki/concepts/stripe-checkout.md:145 omit that qualification; the source should state the November capture's preview access requirement while preserving its April date and provenance.

The current source lines 13 and 20 and concept line 145 assert a concrete checkout.sessions.update call with customer parameter. Neither old raw lines 4-8 nor new raw lines 5-20 shows that call or identifies an API version or supported integration surface. This is a baseline summary overreach, not a November raw change.

The current source frontmatter lines 1-9 and Raw Sources lines 32-34 reference only the April capture; a reviewed update would add the new raw reference and retain the old one, with both capture dates visible.
substantive_changes: New raw lines 11-20 explicitly labels the feature a preview and provides a form-equivalent access-request example; old raw lines 4-8 had no access wording. This changes the availability qualification, not the documented Customer-to-Session behavior.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The 2026-04-21 old raw lines 4-8 already describes mid-checkout Customer attachment, guest login, auto-population and preservation; retain it as dated historical evidence even while adding the November preview qualifier.
The existing source's 2026-04-21 date and raw file reference at lines 4-7 and 34 should remain attributed to that earlier capture rather than being silently replaced by the November capture.
conflicts: Current source lines 13 and 20 and concept line 145 present checkout.sessions.update(id, { customer: ... }) as a documented integration call, but neither pinned raw capture supplies that API syntax. A reciprocal source/concept warning or correction should distinguish the documented behavioral statement from the unverified method call.

Current source lines 11-26 and concept line 145 present availability without the preview request-access qualification now explicit in new raw lines 11-20; associated index and company routes should reflect it if those descriptions are updated.
unresolved_questions: The pinned captures do not establish which API method, version, server surface or access entitlement implements attachment after Session creation; the linked API reference pages were not part of this evidence packet.
The preview request example in new raw lines 15-20 does not establish that a request is approved, that a Stripe account has access, or that a checkout/payment outcome succeeded.

findings: New raw lines 11-20 adds a preview access request missing from source lines 11-26.
Source lines 13 and 20 specify checkout.sessions.update although old raw lines 4-8 and new raw lines 5-20 provide only behavioral prose, not API syntax.
Source frontmatter lines 4-7 and Raw Sources line 34 cite only the older capture; preserve it and add the November raw provenance.
conflicts: The source's uncaveated API call and availability wording conflict with the limited pinned authority and November preview gate; the related concept line 145 repeats the API call.
source_assessments.reason: The new access qualification is material and the current summary overstates concrete integration syntax independently of the raw delta.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/update-customer, new raw lines 5-20 describe attaching a Customer to an existing Checkout Session after creation when a guest logs in during checkout. Saved payment methods, email and billing information then populate without erasing entered information. The new capture explicitly calls this a preview requiring an access request; request submission is not access approval. Old raw lines 4-8 documents the same core behavior without that preview gate. The mapped source-stripe-checkout-update-customer.md captures the core behavior but omits the new qualification and names a specific update API call absent from both pinned raws.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/update-customer, the substantive change is the preview request-access section at new raw lines 11-20; the guest-login wording change from old raw lines 4-8 to new raw lines 5-9 is editorial. Preserve the older capture's April 2026 provenance and behavior in source-stripe-checkout-update-customer.md while adding November evidence. Its checkout.sessions.update syntax, echoed in stripe-checkout.md, needs a reciprocal qualification because neither pinned page documents it. The registration curl is an access request, not a Checkout integration call or proof of account enablement, payment success or settlement; no API version, SDK, or client-server route is established.
